newsitem.title: UK: EMU to force price falls, transparency - study.
newsitem.headline: EMU to force price falls, transparency - study.

text.p: Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) will create transparency and drive prices lower in Europe, according to a study by KPMG Management Consulting.

In many markets competition will not tolerate prices above the average, leading in some cases to "lowest common denominator" pricing, where prices gravitate to the lowest prices currently charged, according to KPMG.

"The introduction of the euro will mean price transparency in the eurozone and is likely to lead to intense buyer pressure on vendors to fix a common price between member states," said Michael Littlechild, a strategy partner at KPMG Management Consulting.
"High cost producers should be prepared to see their margins cut substantially, with a resulting reduction in profitability."
Price transparency will benefit companies that are consumers of goods and services, he said.

"At the moment, a small price difference in the cost of supply can easily be outweighed by the currency risk and this may dissuade a purchaser from automatically switching to the cheapest supplier," Littlechild said.
He also said that there may be a snowball effect, in which the most powerful consumers of goods and services force other consumers to follow suit. REUTER
